paragraphs.source_en: The magnificent Gifu Castle rose from the Senjōdai residence at the foot of Mount Inaba. Its sturdy walls of massive stones stood half-hidden among green trees, bathed in the spring sunshine.

units.source_en: The magnificent Gifu Castle rose from the Senjōdai residence at the foot of Mount Inaba.
units.source_zh: 壮观的岐阜城起自稻叶山麓的千叠台馆阁。

units.source_en: Its sturdy walls of massive stones stood half-hidden among green trees, bathed in the spring sunshine.
units.source_zh: 巨石垒成的坚固城墙，掩映在绿树之中，沐浴着春日的阳光。

paragraphs.source_zh: 壮观的岐阜城起自稻叶山麓的千叠台馆阁。巨石垒成的坚固城墙，掩映在绿树之中，沐浴着春日的阳光。

paragraphs.source_en: Paulo, a Portuguese missionary visiting the castle for the first time, described Gifu Castle in a letter to the missionary Figueiredo in Bungo: “Great stones are piled one upon another, yet no plaster is to be seen; it can only be the work of gods and demons.” He even said that Gifu Castle was larger than the residence of the Portuguese viceroy in India at the time.

units.source_en: Paulo, a Portuguese missionary visiting the castle for the first time, described Gifu Castle in a letter to the missionary Figueiredo in Bungo: “Great stones are piled one upon another, yet no plaster is to be seen; it can only be the work of gods and demons.”
units.source_zh: 首次造访此城的葡国（葡萄牙）传教士保罗，在寄给丰后的传教士菲盖莱德的信中如此描述岐阜城：“巨石层叠，灰泥绝见，只当鬼斧神工。”

units.source_en: He even said that Gifu Castle was larger than the residence of the Portuguese viceroy in India at the time.
units.source_zh: 他甚至说，岐阜城比当时的葡国驻天竺总督的官邸还要大。

paragraphs.source_zh: 首次造访此城的葡国（葡萄牙）传教士保罗，在寄给丰后的传教士菲盖莱德的信中如此描述岐阜城：“巨石层叠，灰泥绝见，只当鬼斧神工。”他甚至说，岐阜城比当时的葡国驻天竺总督的官邸还要大。

paragraphs.source_en: In the courtyard of Senjōdai, pear blossoms billowed like rosy mist. Just returned from the capital, Princess Nō entered the formidable castle gate without a word, crossed the residence and a grove of pear trees, and came into the inner garden.

units.source_en: In the courtyard of Senjōdai, pear blossoms billowed like rosy mist.
units.source_zh: 千叠台的庭院中，梨花如烟霞。

units.source_en: Just returned from the capital, Princess Nō entered the formidable castle gate without a word, crossed the residence and a grove of pear trees, and came into the inner garden.
units.source_zh: 刚从京城回来的浓姬一声不吭地走进坚固的城门，穿过府邸，经过一片梨花林，来到内庭。

paragraphs.source_zh: 千叠台的庭院中，梨花如烟霞。刚从京城回来的浓姬一声不吭地走进坚固的城门，穿过府邸，经过一片梨花林，来到内庭。

paragraphs.source_en: Lady Nō seldom lost her composure like this. She merely glanced at the concubines who had hurried out in confusion to greet her, went straight to her bedchamber, summoned her maid Tamao, and asked softly, “Someone seems to have come to the council chamber in the outer court, is that right?”

units.source_en: Lady Nō seldom lost her composure like this.

ja.t: すことはめったになかった。

units.source_zh: 浓夫人很少如此失态。

units.source_en: She merely glanced at the concubines who had hurried out in confusion to greet her, went straight to her bedchamber, summoned her maid Tamao, and asked softly, “Someone seems to have come to the council chamber in the outer court, is that right?”
units.source_zh: 她只扫了一眼慌慌张张跑出来迎接的妾室，径直走向自己的卧房，叫过侍女玉绪，低声问：“似乎有人到外庭议事房来了，是吗？”

paragraphs.source_en: “Yes...but I do not know who it is.”

units.source_en: “Yes...but I do not know who it is.”
units.source_zh: “是……但不清楚是什么人。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “是……但不清楚是什么人。”

paragraphs.source_en: “You do not know who it is? You are far too careless. Fukutomi Heizaemon should be on duty today. Bring him to me.”

paragraphs.source_en: After Tamao hurried out, O-Nagisa brushed past her and set a tea bowl before her lady. Princess Nō took it and looked up at the pear blossoms filling the courtyard. Her husband, Nobunaga, had not yet withdrawn from Kanegasaki Castle. “How worrying...” she murmured to herself.

units.source_en: Princess Nō took it and looked up at the pear blossoms filling the courtyard.

units.source_en: Her husband, Nobunaga, had not yet withdrawn from Kanegasaki Castle.

units.source_en: “How worrying...” she murmured to herself.
units.source_zh: “真让人担心……”她自言自语着。

paragraphs.source_zh: 玉绪慌慌张张退出后，阿渚和玉绪擦肩而过，将茶碗放在夫人面前。浓姬接过，抬头看着满院盛开的梨花。丈夫信长还未撤出金崎城。“真让人担心……”她自言自语着。

paragraphs.source_en: Before her very eyes, this castle built by her father had changed hands four times. First came her father; then Yoshitatsu, who killed him; after that Yoshitatsu’s son Tatsuoki; and now her husband, Nobunaga.

units.source_en: Before her very eyes, this castle built by her father had changed hands four times.
units.source_zh: 她眼睁睁看着父亲建起的这座城池四易其主。

units.source_en: First came her father; then Yoshitatsu, who killed him; after that Yoshitatsu’s son Tatsuoki; and now her husband, Nobunaga.
units.source_zh: 先是父亲，次是杀死父亲的义龙，接下来是义龙的儿子龙兴，现在是丈夫信长。

paragraphs.source_zh: 她眼睁睁看着父亲建起的这座城池四易其主。先是父亲，次是杀死父亲的义龙，接下来是义龙的儿子龙兴，现在是丈夫信长。

paragraphs.source_en: On the day Nobunaga departed from Sakamoto, Shogun Yoshiaki sent a messenger to the home of Nakarai Roan, where Princess Nō was staying, inviting her to tea. Delighted, Princess Nō went in the company of Asayama Nichijō.

units.source_en: On the day Nobunaga departed from Sakamoto, Shogun Yoshiaki sent a messenger to the home of Nakarai Roan, where Princess Nō was staying, inviting her to tea.
units.source_zh: 信长从坂本出发当日，将军义昭派人到浓姬居住的半井庐庵家中，邀请她去品茶。

units.source_en: Delighted, Princess Nō went in the company of Asayama Nichijō.
units.source_zh: 浓姬高兴地在朝山日乘的陪同下前去了。

paragraphs.source_zh: 信长从坂本出发当日，将军义昭派人到浓姬居住的半井庐庵家中，邀请她去品茶。浓姬高兴地在朝山日乘的陪同下前去了。

paragraphs.source_en: The shogun’s new Nijō Castle residence had been built by Nobunaga at enormous expense to reassure the people and presented directly to Yoshiaki upon completion. Princess Nō had even heard that the shogun himself had poured sake for Nobunaga at the celebratory banquet. That was precisely why she had gone without the slightest suspicion, only to sense upon arriving that something was amiss.

units.source_en: The shogun’s new Nijō Castle residence had been built by Nobunaga at enormous expense to reassure the people and presented directly to Yoshiaki upon completion.
units.source_zh: 将军的二条城新宅，是信长为了安定人心斥巨资所建，落成后直接献给了义昭。

units.source_en: Princess Nō had even heard that the shogun himself had poured sake for Nobunaga at the celebratory banquet.
units.source_zh: 浓姬甚至听说将军在庆祝宴会上亲自给信长斟酒。

units.source_en: That was precisely why she had gone without the slightest suspicion, only to sense upon arriving that something was amiss.
units.source_zh: 正因如此，她才毫无戒心地过去了，但抵达后才发觉气氛不对。

paragraphs.source_zh: 将军的二条城新宅，是信长为了安定人心斥巨资所建，落成后直接献给了义昭。浓姬甚至听说将军在庆祝宴会上亲自给信长斟酒。正因如此，她才毫无戒心地过去了，但抵达后才发觉气氛不对。

paragraphs.source_en: Princess Nō was no stranger to hard experience; she was not one to lose her head in such a tense atmosphere. The missionaries called Nobunaga the King of Gifu and Princess Nō his queen; indeed, tempered by long years of experience, she possessed a queenly dignity. Compared with Lady Tsukiyama, who had grown still more ignorant after childbirth, she possessed an incomparable strength.

units.source_en: Princess Nō was no stranger to hard experience; she was not one to lose her head in such a tense atmosphere.

paragraphs.source_en: In a temporary tearoom erected near the Kushanhakkai garden at Nijō Castle, besides the host, Shogun Yoshiaki, were Hino, the Major Counselor, and Takakura, the Councillor; Hosokawa Fujitaka and Mitsubuchi Yamato-no-kami had also been invited. Princess Nō took her seat with neither servility nor arrogance.

units.source_en: In a temporary tearoom erected near the Kushanhakkai garden at Nijō Castle, besides the host, Shogun Yoshiaki, were Hino, the Major Counselor, and Takakura, the Councillor; Hosokawa Fujitaka and Mitsubuchi Yamato-no-kami had also been invited.

units.source_en: Princess Nō took her seat with neither servility nor arrogance.
units.source_zh: 浓姬不卑不亢地落座了。

paragraphs.source_en: “Your Excellency is gravely mistaken. This new residence symbolizes the revival of the Ashikaga clan. Before all else, you should join Nobunaga in seeking dominion over the realm.”

paragraphs.source_en: “With respect, those are not words a shogun should speak. The realm is in chaos. If Your Excellency is powerless to act, then you should uphold Nobunaga, who risks his life and all he possesses to pacify it.”
